title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to Grothendieck's L-function notes. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 392, page 4-36) for Commutative Algebra ch. VII 'Diviseurs', §4 on pseudo-null modules, the characteristic divisor χ, the Chern class c and the rank r. It was presumably reused as scrap paper; the handwritten L-function computations on the neighbouring pages are unrelated to it.

Setting: A is an integrally closed noetherian domain (Krull-type) and B is a finite extension domain of A, e.g. the integral closure of A in a finite separable extension of its fraction field. For a height-≤1 prime p of A, B_p is a finite torsion-free module over the DVR A_p. The map i : D(A) → D(B) (and on class groups) is the extension of divisors.

The page first finishes the proof of Prop. 19 (an intersection-of-localizations argument, via Lemma 4 and n°2 Th. 2).

Proposition 20:
(i) A finitely generated A-module M is pseudo-null iff M⊗_A B is pseudo-null over B.
(ii) If M is a finitely generated torsion module, then χ_B(M⊗_A B) = i(χ_A(M)).
(iii) For finitely generated M, c_B(M⊗_A B) = i(c_A(M)) and r_B(M⊗_A B) = r_A(M).

Proof of (i): For a prime P of B with p = P∩A, (M⊗_A B)_P = M_p ⊗_{A_p} B_P. Since A_p → B_P is local and M_p is finitely generated, Nakayama gives M_p = 0 iff (M⊗B)_P = 0. Apply this to P = 0 (torsion) and to the height-1 primes P (pseudo-nullity, via n°4 Prop. 9).

Lemma 5: If f : M_1 → M_2 is an injective map of finitely generated A-modules, then ker(f⊗1_B) is pseudo-null. Localize at a height-≤1 prime p of A. A_p is a PID (field or DVR), so B_p is finite torsion-free, hence free, hence flat. Therefore f_p⊗1 is injective. The proof continues on the next typed page, not included here.

The lemma is used to show that χ, which is additive up to pseudo-null modules, commutes with base change.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Proof of (i), direction 'M⊗B pseudo-null ⇒ M pseudo-null': it implicitly needs every height-≤1 prime p of A to have a prime P of B of height ≤1 lying over it. This holds by lying-over and incomparability for the finite (integral) extension, but it is not stated on this page; presumably it is covered by n°4 Prop. 9 or the standing hypotheses.

ideas.what: Pseudo-nullity of finitely generated modules is detected after extension to a finite (integral) extension B of A
ideas.modern_name: Pseudo-null modules under integral base change (Bourbaki AC VII §4)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative ch. VII §4 (extension of scalars)

ideas.what: Compatibility of characteristic divisor, Chern class and rank with base change: χ_B(M⊗B) = i(χ_A(M)), c_B = i∘c_A, r_B = r_A
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of characteristic ideal / first Chern class of modules over Krull domains

ideas.what: Injectivity of f⊗1_B holds up to a pseudo-null kernel, because B is free over the DVR localizations A_p

In the first displayed formula the left side is ∩_{P∈P(B)} R_P and the right side is ∩_{p∈P(A)} (R[A])_p as transcribed; 'R[A]' is read from the image, but its exact meaning (likely a ring R with a bracketed subscript) is uncertain.
